appraisal_events.evidence: il est devenu d'une beauté, il a l'air d'une espèce de Bronzino, il est vraiment admirable; the elaborate scheme to invite Oriane and other society figures so that le nom de Morel revient tout le temps et finit par se graver dans la mémoire; Charlus arranging through Bergotte for Morel to publish music chronicles, a talent that peut un jour acquérir le prestige de celui de Berlioz.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus works elaborately, through personal praise and stage-managed high-society publicity, to elevate Morel's reputation as violinist, composer, and writer, though the narrator frames this doting as vain and self-serving, like an old conservatory stage-mother.

appraisal_events.evidence: on verra plus tard que cette presse verbale réduisit à néant la puissance d'un Charlus devenu démodé et, bien au-dessus de lui, érigea un Morel qui ne valait pas la millionième partie de son ancien protecteur; cette mode intellectuelle...croit de bonne foi au néant d'un génial Charlus, à l'incontestable autorité d'un stupide Morel.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly foretells that the very publicity machine Charlus builds for Morel will eventually destroy Charlus's own social power and elevate an undeserving Morel far above him.

appraisal_events.evidence: il faisait faire à Morel...des petits entrefilets bassement calomniateurs et dirigés contre la comtesse Molé...des passages de lettres d'elle, textuellement cités, mais pris dans un sens où ils pouvaient l'affoler comme la plus cruelle vengeance. La jeune femme en mourut.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus secretly has Morel publish calumnious paragraphs against comtesse Molé, twisting her own private letters against her with such cruelty that she dies from the ordeal; the narrator condemns this as one of Charlus's implacable vengeances.

status_effects.explanation: Morel's reputation is actively and visibly built up through Charlus's praise and orchestrated society publicity.
The narrator states plainly that this same promotional machine will later destroy Charlus's own standing while elevating Morel far beyond his merit.
Comtesse Molé's reputation is publicly destroyed by calumnious press paragraphs orchestrated by Charlus, with fatal consequences for her.
The narrator explicitly judges Charlus's implacable, underhanded vengeance against comtesse Molé as morally damning.

ambiguities: Charlus's praise of Morel is sincere in his own voice but is framed by the narrator with irony ('vieilles mamans-gâteau du Conservatoire'), complicating whether the elevation should be read as fully endorsed.
